Think of it like a set of Russian nesting dolls: to open the biggest doll, you first open the next smaller one, and so on until you reach the smallest doll, which is the base case that stops the process. In short, recursion breaks a big problem into identical, smaller chunks until the answer becomes trivial, then builds the final answer back up.
